sources.title: Monumenta Orientalia, Italian-French excavations at Tamnaʿ
sources.note: Direct excavation project report: campaigns 1999 to 2009, Sector A Athirat temple, Sector B houses and inscriptions. Broad destruction dating first to second century CE. No automatic equation of fire with conquest.

sources.title: Julien Charbonnier, The control of water in the kingdom of Qatabān, Water History 7 (2015), 473 to 487
sources.note: Publisher abstract directly read; author-uploaded full text read at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/283914044_The_control_of_water_in_the_kingdom_of_Qataban_Yemen_from_local_to_central_management_of_the_irrigation_systems_during_antiquity . Same work for budgeting. Food p. 479; family well p. 480; upstream decree pp. 480 to 482. Crop list is site-wide, not one securely dated meal.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art, Pair of lions with riders
sources.note: Indexed original full exhibition text retrieved by query site:asia-archive.si.edu/exhibition/pair-of-lions-with-riders "comb". Direct page intermittently fails. House Yafash finds and sculpture catalogue 75 BCE to 50 CE, LTS1992.6.87/88. Count all pages of Unearthing Arabia exhibition as one work.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The World between Empires (2019), Southwestern Arabia, p. 29
sources.note: Indexed original PDF p. 29 verified with query site:resources.metmuseum.org "Timna" "loculi". Direct fetch failed. Same work already used by Seleucid kingdom; cumulative budget includes that card. TT1 interpretation distinguished from secure Athirat temple in Sector A.

sources.title: Toledo Museum of Art, Funerary Statuette of Abī-yadaʿ, 2023.340
sources.note: Direct object record, third century BCE, 47 cm; exact scholarly Latin transliteration and museum translation. Probable cemetery provenance, not secure excavated context. References RES 3896 (13), CSAI I no. 784. Museum historical label dates annexation first century CE, differing from French project second century; public copy gives broad first to second-century transition and flags disagreement.

proposedOverrides.name: Qataban
proposedOverrides.summary: Qataban’s South Arabian kingdom linked irrigated valleys, named urban households and regulated incense markets.

batchIdentityNotes.notes: Exact indexed missing record checked; no alias. Four identical decoded southern-Yemen outlines at 323, 300, 200 and 100 BCE end at 1 BCE. No precise historical border endorsed. Public caveat distinguishes these snapshots from longer kingdom. Saba/Hadramawt cards remain separate. First to second-century CE domestic finds clearly labelled beyond map endpoint. Museum first-century annexation and French project second-century chronology acknowledged; no unsupported exact fell link. Writing is attested transliteration, not fabricated original glyphs. No evidence-backed school system, medical treatment or household toilets found in these checked sources, so none asserted.
